1.why: All screens use a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable line height and clear contrast.

2.why: Instructions are brief sentence-case lines without italics; capitals appear only in the brand mark and the code/secret strings themselves.

3.why: The single-column layout fits phone width, but the otpauth URI wraps mid-string and up to eight stacked error banners push the form below the fold.

4.why: Directions are one or two plain sentences each, though phrases like 'provisioning representation' and 'manual secret' are technical.

5.why: Only the recovery-code input shows an example format (ABCD-EFGH-JKLM placeholder); the verification-code and authenticator-code fields show none.

6.why: The user must read the dense, ever-growing monospace Logs panel to obtain the verification code, authenticator code, and recovery codes.

7.why: Secrets and codes are rendered as plain selectable text that can be copied, though no explicit copy button is provided.

8.why: No QR code is ever rendered; the 'scan' option is only a raw otpauth:// URI text that still must be copied by hand.

9.why: The username/password pair is a standard form a password manager can fill, but no autocomplete or one-time-code affordances are visible on any code field.

10.why: Every screen pairs a bold step heading (e.g., 'Verify your identity') with one full-width green primary button that clearly stands out.

11.why: Each screen requests a single primary action, with other options demoted to quiet links or a grey secondary button.

12.why: Success screens state what happened and what comes next, but failures only stack 'Unable to continue sign-in.' banners or a raw insertBefore DOM error with no guidance.

13.why: Sign-in can be retried repeatedly without lockout and replacement codes can be generated, but there is no reveal/hide toggle and no resend-code control.

14.why: Error banners ('Unable to continue sign-in.', raw JS exception) never explain the cause or the fix, even though they avoid blaming the user.

15.why: The UI itself states 'Codes rotate every 30 seconds' and calls the verification code short-lived, so code entry is tightly time-boxed.
